statement: For the integral Weierstrass equation y²+a1xy+a3y=x³+a2x²+a4x+a6, the displayed b-invariants, c4,c6 and discriminant are integer polynomials; 4b8=b2b6−b4² and c4³−c6²=1728Δ hold over Z. The smooth locus is Δ invertible and ω=dx/(2y+a1x+a3). Over a ring in which 6 is invertible the equation becomes Y²=4X³−(c4/12)X−c6/216.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: work/code/c63_algebra.py: invariant_residuals and coordinate_substitution_residual are identically zero. The smoothness assertion uses the Jacobian criterion, not just the polynomial identity.
fate: Classical Weierstrass invariant theory; the same integral formulas are recorded in Tate1975 §1 and Deligne1975 §1. These are collected texts by Tate, not an unpublished theorem of Grothendieck.
fate_date: Known before these undated archival copies; printed in 1975.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established, with the printed formula alarms separated in the reading register.

statement: Every origin-preserving isomorphism between Weierstrass equations has the indicated admissible coordinate form with u a unit. The a_i transformation formulas, b_i shifts, weights 4,6,12 for c4,c6,Δ and ω=u^−1ω′ follow by substitution. For j(j−1728) invertible the displayed generic equation has c4=j/(j−1728), c6=−j/(j−1728), and that j-invariant.
status_on_pages: false as stated: the generic model has the wrong sign for c6; the coordinate-change formulas otherwise agree
computation: c63_algebra.py verifies every displayed invariant transformation by polynomial substitution and computes the generic model; residual j_reconstruction=J. Refined record C-SA16-803.
fate: Tate1975 §2 and Deligne1975 §1 give the coordinate changes. The generic model requires the negative c6 sign independently calculated here.
present_status: As of November 2026: Use the corrected c6 sign, without altering the diplomatic transcription.

statement: Refinement of C-SA16-802: y²+xy=x³−36x/(J−1728)−1/(J−1728) has c4=J/(J−1728), c6=−J/(J−1728), Δ=J²/(J−1728)³. This representative is defined where J and J−1728 are invertible; choosing it does not classify all twists over a nonclosed field.
status_on_pages: false as stated, corrected here as a reconstruction
computation: Exact substitution in c63_algebra.py; taking J=1 gives c4=−1/1727, c6=1/1727, so the two are not equal in Q.
fate: The model is the standard generic j representative; its twist caveat is part of the coarse-moduli distinction.
present_status: As of November 2026: Corrected identity established by exact calculation.

his_statement: A minimal equation exists and is unique up to ...
statement: Over a discrete valuation ring R with fraction field K, an elliptic curve with an integral Weierstrass equation has a minimal discriminant valuation; two minimal equations differ by an admissible transformation with u∈R× and r,s,t∈R. The resulting differential is defined up to R×. The global minimal-discriminant ideal represents the twelfth power of the Hodge-line class; a PID permits a global minimal equation.
status_on_pages: proof sketched
computation: The valuation of Δ changes by 12v(u), checked symbolically in C-SA16-802. Existence is well-ordering of nonnegative valuations; the integrality of the transition parameters is the substantive local minimal-model theorem, carried from Tate1975 §3.
fate: Tate1975 §3 gives the local minimal equation theorem and the obstruction over a general Dedekind base.
fate_date: Letter predates 1975 publication; exact circulation date not supplied.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with the stated local/global distinction.

his_statement: ord Δ<12 ... si j est entier ...
statement: An integral equation with v(Δ)<12 is minimal. If j is integral and the residue characteristic is not 2 or 3, minimality implies v(Δ)<12. The displayed wider bound v(Δ)<12+12v(2)+6v(3) concerns minimal equations with integral j, and is not a bound for multiplicative reduction with arbitrary v(j)<0.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: The sufficient direction follows from Δ-weight12; necessity outside 2,3 follows from the additive Kodaira valuations. The wild bound is used as a background result, not claimed proved by a finite coefficient test.
fate: Tate1975 §3 gives the minimality bounds; §§7–8 give the algorithm, including the wild residue characteristics.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established under the integral-j hypothesis; omitting it gives split multiplicative counterexamples of arbitrarily large minimal discriminant.

statement: For a minimal Weierstrass equation over a complete DVR with perfect residue field, reduction identifies E0(K)/E1(K) with the nonsingular special-fiber group; this is an elliptic curve, a split or nonsplit torus, or Ga according to reduction. For P near infinity, z=−x/y has v(z)=m>0, v(x)=−2m,v(y)=−3m. The formal filtration has Em/Em+1≅additive residue field; surjectivity of lifting uses completeness/Henselian hypotheses. In addition, E0(K) has finite index in E(K), as stated in Theorem4.1 on scan7. This component-group finiteness does not require a finite residue field, whereas the reduction quotient E0(K)/E1(K) can be infinite when the residue field is infinite.
status_on_pages: proof sketched
computation: The valuations follow from x=z/w, y=−1/w, w=z³+O(z⁴). The additive associated-graded law follows from the linear term of the formal group. No claim of surjectivity over a non-Henselian DVR is made.
fate: Tate1975 §§3–4 matches the filtration and formal-parameter construction.
present_status: As of November2026: Established. The component quotient E(K)/E0(K) is finite under these hypotheses; finiteness of the residue field is needed for the finite point-count and Haar-volume setting, not for Theorem4.1’s component index.

statement: There is a unique formal solution w∈z³R[[z]] of the displayed equation. It produces the Weierstrass formal group in z and expansions x=z^−2−a1z^−1−a2−a3z−(a1a3+a4)z²+… and ω=(1+a1z+(a1²+a2)z²+(a1³+2a1a2+2a3)z³+…)dz. The line-intersection formula uses w=λz+ν and Vieta in the z roots.
status_on_pages: false as stated at two coefficients/signs; construction is sketched
computation: c63_algebra.py computes w through z9, x through z2 and ω through z3, and the exact cubic root-sum formula. The transcription has a3 instead of 2a3 in ω, and two wrong initial signs in the Vieta numerator.
fate: Tate1975 §4 gives the formal-group construction. The displayed algebra is independently checked here rather than inferred from the later source.
present_status: As of November 2026: Construction established; use the explicitly corrected formulas in the computation output.

statement: Over a nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field of q elements, normalize |ω| by a minimal invariant differential and additive Haar measure so R has measure1. Then vol(E1)=q^−1, vol(E0)=#Ẽns(k)/q=Lv(1)^−1, and vol(E(K))=cv/Lv(1), where cv=[E:E0]. The Euler factors are 1−aT+qT² for good,1−T for split multiplicative,1+T for nonsplit multiplicative,1 for additive reduction.
status_on_pages: proved there
computation: c63_kodaira.py verifies the four exact point-count/Euler-factor identities. Each reduction coset has minimal-differential volume 1/q; multiplication by the component index gives the total volume.
fate: Tate1975 §5 gives precisely this measure normalization and formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with finite residue field and minimal-differential normalization.

his_statement: I0, Iν, II, III, IV, I0*, Iν*, IV*, III*, II*
statement: For an elliptic curve over a complete DVR with algebraically closed residue field, the minimal regular proper model has the ten Kodaira fiber families displayed. Their geometric component counts are 1,n,1,2,3,5,n+5,7,8,9. The smooth Néron model is obtained by removing the non-smooth parts; it is not the same scheme as the proper regular model. The geometric component groups are 1,Z/n,1,Z/2,Z/3,(Z/2)², Z/4 for odd n and (Z/2)² for even n, Z/3,Z/2,1.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: c63_kodaira.py checks the affine component counts and computes Smith normal forms of the associated A, D and E Cartan matrices. It covers I_n and I_n* for 1≤n≤20 and every exceptional type. The lattice-to-component-group identification is carried from the geometric classification, not established merely by drawing a graph.
fate: The Kodaira/Néron classification is reproduced in Tate1975 §6; §§7–8 give its effective tests.
fate_date: Classification predates letter; Tate algorithm printed1975.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established. Arithmetic Tamagawa numbers may be smaller than geometric component-group orders.

statement: For an elliptic curve over a complete DVR with perfect residue field, Ogg’s formula is f=v(Δ_min)+1−m, where m counts geometric irreducible components. Outside residue characteristics 2 and 3 the additive discriminant valuations are 2,3,4,6,n+6,8,9,10. In the additive case f=2 and p≠2,3, multiplication by 12 is an automorphism of E0(K): this follows from its formal subgroup and additive reduction quotient. Since E(K)/E0(K) is killed by 12, the natural map E(K)[12]→E(K)/E0(K) is an isomorphism. The additive hypothesis is essential.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: c63_kodaira.py checks f=0,1,2 for the good, multiplicative and tame additive rows. The 12-torsion assertion is independently proved: for any coset represented by P, solve 12Q=12P uniquely in E0(K), giving the unique 12-torsion lift P−Q. No finite table is substituted for the wild Ogg theorem.
fate: Tate1975 §6 records Ogg’s conductor formula and the exceptional residue characteristics.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established; the transcription inequality p=2 or3 where the tame table is used must be checked on the scan.

his_statement: Algorithm ... complete discrete valuation ring ... perfect residue field
statement: Tate’s algorithm tests an integral Weierstrass model, in a cumulative sequence of translations, coefficient valuations, a normalized cubic and subsequent quadratic tests, and returns Kodaira type, minimal discriminant, conductor and component index over a complete DVR with perfect residue field. If all terminal minimality tests fail, scaling (a1,a2,a3,a4,a6) by powers(1,2,3,4,6) lowers vΔ by12 and restarts. Nonsplit multiplicative reduction is identified by the nontrivial quadratic residue extension.
status_on_pages: proof sketched
computation: Scaling and the cubic/quadratic discriminant formulas are exactly checked in c63_algebra.py. Termination follows from decreasing vΔ on restart and bounded component count during a fixed minimal branch. The full algorithm’s geometric correctness is carried from Tate1975 §§7–8, not claimed independently re-proved.
fate: The copied letter is the source of Tate1975, Algorithm for determining the type of a singular fiber in an elliptic pencil, pp33–52. The matching later publication is by Tate, hence classB relative to Grothendieck’s corpus.
fate_date: Earlier letter circulated to Cassels; exact date not recovered from the supplied pages. Publication1975.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established for the stated hypotheses. This dossier does not extend it to imperfect residue fields.

his_statement: courbes de genre1 ... section dans le lieu lisse
statement: For a proper flat finitely presented family of geometrically integral reduced curves of arithmetic genus1 with a section e in the smooth locus, e is an effective Cartier divisor. For n>0, R¹p*O(ne)=0 and p*O(ne) is locally free of rank n, compatible with arbitrary base change; p*O=p*O(e)=OS. The graded pieces for n≥2 are ω^−n, where ω=e*Ω¹C/S.
status_on_pages: proof sketched
computation: Fiberwise Riemann–Roch and Serre duality: a negative-degree invertible sheaf has no sections on a geometrically integral proper curve; cohomology/base change gives the family statement. The n=1 quotient is zero and must not be confused with the n≥2 formula.
fate: Deligne1968 preprint M/68/28, then Deligne1975 §1, is the same authored text; the proof uses standard cohomology and base change.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established for integral fibers; arbitrary reducible generalized elliptic curves require a modified formulation.

statement: Such genus-one plane-cubic fibers are Gorenstein; their relative dualizing sheaf is canonically the pullback of ω after normalization along e. Evaluation p*p*Ωreg→Ωreg is an isomorphism because a nonzero regular differential on an integral arithmetic-genus-one curve has no zero. The notation Rp! and the indexing in the transcription require its cohomological convention to be checked, not a forced replacement by an ordinary cotangent sheaf at a node.
status_on_pages: open on the pages: marginal verification request
computation: The fiberwise degree-zero argument and base change prove the evaluation assertion under C-SA16-812 hypotheses; no equality with the singular Kähler differential sheaf is used.
fate: Deligne1975 §1 and Grothendieck duality supply the family dualizing interpretation.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established in the Gorenstein/dualizing formulation; the transcription’s derived-degree convention remains an ink question.

statement: Locally trivializing ω and choosing normalized bases in p*O(2e),p*O(3e) produces x,y with pole orders2,3, a unique relation y²+a1xy+a3y=x³+a2x²+a4x+a6, and a plane-cubic embedding from O(3e). The distinguished point is the flex at infinity. Different choices are related by the admissible coordinate group.
status_on_pages: proof sketched
computation: Riemann–Roch dimensions1,2,3,6 in degrees1,2,3,6 force the unique relation after monomial normalization. Homogenizing the equation makes the line at infinity meet at e with multiplicity3.
fate: Deligne1968/1975 §1 is the published construction.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established locally on the base; global x,y require line-bundle trivializations.

statement: The auxiliary invariants d6=b2b4−18b6 and d8=b2²b4−48b4²+18b2b6 satisfy the displayed identities and Δ=b4³−27b6²+b8(36b4−b2²). Coordinate-shift formulas follow from the Weierstrass substitution; the discriminant of the completed-square cubic is16Δ.
status_on_pages: open on the pages at the exponent check; otherwise stated
computation: All polynomial identities have zero exact residual in c63_algebra.py. The exponent b2² in the second discriminant expression is correct. The alternate a4 formula requires −F_x rather than −F.
fate: These are elementary consequences of the classical integral invariant formulas, also present in Deligne1975 §1.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established as polynomial identities over Z.

statement: Over Z[1/6], integral reduced genus-one curves with smooth marked origin and a nowhere-zero invariant differential are represented by the affine (g2,g3)-plane via Y²=4X³−g2X−g3. Smooth elliptic curves are its open Δ≠0; the nodal and cuspidal points remain in the larger genus-one moduli problem. The marking is[0:1:0] and ω=dX/Y.
status_on_pages: proof sketched with marginal question at the canonical section
computation: Completing square and eliminating the quadratic term gives the unique normalized equation, verified by the coordinate formulas. At the marked point ∂F/∂Z≠0, including singular finite fibers.
fate: Deligne1975 §2, pp.58–59, gives this rigidified normal form.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established for the stated enlarged genus-one functor; it is not the smooth elliptic moduli space unless Δ is inverted.

statement: When2 and c4 are invertible, the equation can be uniquely gauged to a1=a3=0 and d6=0 after choosing the differential. Then a2a4=9a6, a2c4=−c6/4, a4c4²=−36Δ, a6c4³=c6Δ; these equations describe the ordinary c4-open normal form.
status_on_pages: open on the pages at uniqueness/existence; formulas given
computation: Exact substitution into the invariant definitions verifies all four identities in c63_more_algebra.py. The translation changes d6 by a unit multiple of c4, so the required r is unique when c4 is invertible.
fate: Deligne1975 §3, p.60, gives this gauge on the open where 2 and c4 are units.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with2,c4 units and a chosen differential.

statement: On the ordinary c4-open in characteristic2, a normalized equation is y²+xy=x³+a2x²+a6, with c4=c6=1 and Δ=a6; residual changes are Artin–Schreier changes in a2. Over an algebraically closed field the supersingular models are y²+y=x³ in characteristic2 and y²=x³−x in characteristic3. The respective discriminants are a3⁴ and−a4³ in the unnormalized special forms.
status_on_pages: stated without proof; normalizations explained
computation: Direct reduction of the invariant polynomials modulo2 and3 and coordinate changes is included in c63_more_algebra.py. Algebraic closedness/separable extensions are needed to solve the normalization equations.
fate: Deligne1975 §4, pp.61–63, treats the characteristic-2 and characteristic-3 normal forms.
fate_date: Classical forms;1968/1975 publication of the text.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with field and trivialization hypotheses; ordinary and supersingular branches must be kept separate.

statement: Over a field, a Weierstrass cubic with its marked smooth point is smooth iffΔ≠0, nodal iffΔ=0 andc4≠0, and cuspidal iffΔ=c4=0. The nodal assertion is geometric; its torus can be nonsplit over the ground field.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: Jacobian and tangent-cone classification reduce to the completed-square cubic when2≠0; characteristic2 is checked in its normal forms. In particular discriminant vanishing alone does not distinguish node from cusp.
fate: Deligne1975 Proposition5.1, p.63, classifies the geometric singularity by Δ and c4; Tate1975 §1 gives the same criterion.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established.

statement: For pointed genus-one curves without additive fibers (smooth or nodal), the Isom functor is finite unramified. Equal j makes its projection surjective on the underlying topological spaces; on the open avoiding0 and1728 it is finite étale of rank2. The page does not claim flatness of Isom at the special j-values. In characteristic2 the ordinary twisting equation is Artin–Schreier; when2 is invertible the generic twist is quadratic.
status_on_pages: proof sketched
computation: The explicit coordinate equations prove finiteness and the absence of infinitesimal origin-preserving automorphisms. The ordinary equation’s a2x term in the transcription must be a2x².
fate: Deligne1975 Proposition5.3, pp.64–65, gives the finite unramified Isom scheme and its surjectivity criterion. Proposition5.4 treats generic quadratic twisting.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established as written, including nodal fibers. An fppf-isomorphism assertion over all special-j nonreduced bases would be stronger and false: y²=x³+εx+1 over C[ε]/ε² has j=0 but is not a twist of the constant j0 curve.

statement: Over an algebraically closed field, the pointed automorphism group has order2 generically; outside characteristic2,3 it is μ6 atj0 andμ4 atj1728; at the supersingular point in characteristic3 it is C3⋊C4 of order12; in characteristic2 it is SL2(F3) of order24 with quaternion kernelQ8 on the differential character. Over disconnected bases, a global section of the constant order2 group can choose signs separately on components, so there are more than two global automorphisms.
status_on_pages: false as stated for a literal two-element set over arbitrary disconnected bases; the margin raises the objection
computation: Counterexample: over S=Spec(C×C), take the same generic-j elliptic curve on both components. The map(+1,−1) is neither global+1 nor global−1. Finite group computations in c63_algebra.py and c63_more_algebra.py check the small-characteristic groups.
fate: Deligne1975 §5, pp.67–68, records these groups. A relative automorphism group scheme need not have only two global sections on a disconnected base.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established after this base-sensitive correction; the displayed composition formula has a separate variable alarm.

statement: The ring of integral level-one modular forms, regular at the cusp, is Z[c4,c6,Δ]/(c4³−c6²−1728Δ), with weights4,6,12. In characteristics2 and3 the corresponding rings are F2[a1,Δ] andF3[b2,Δ], weights1,12 and2,12. Removing the cuspidal/additive locus in the smooth Weierstrass atlas does not change sections when its complement has codimension≥2 and the atlas is normal. Inverting Δ instead gives weakly holomorphic forms and a different ring.
status_on_pages: proof sketched; codimension extension explicitly questioned
computation: The invariant relation is checked exactly; the Hartogs extension argument is a separate normality/codimension proof. The mod3 b2 calculation cannot be assigned toF2 as one marginal label appears to do.
fate: Deligne1975 §6, pp.69–71, gives the integral and exceptional-characteristic rings; Katz1973 supplies the modular interpretation.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with the stated regularity convention.

statement: In characteristic 2 the Hasse section is represented by a1. In characteristic 3 it is represented, up to the sign normalization of Frobenius and the invariant differential, by b2; Deligne1975 Remark6.3 explicitly prints −b2. Both have weight p−1 and cut out the supersingular divisor. The intrinsic definition uses Frobenius/Verschiebung over arbitrary characteristic-p bases. Over a perfect field every ordinary elliptic curve has its Serre–Tate canonical lift to Witt vectors. This does not give a canonical lift for supersingular curves or an unqualified universal coefficient formula.
status_on_pages: open on the pages
computation: Characteristic2/3 Hasse polynomials checked in c63_more_algebra.py; the canonical-lift existence and uniqueness are used from Serre–Tate theory, not claimed proved by coefficient calculations.
fate: Katz1973 §2.0 defines the Hasse invariant functorially; Serre–Tate deformation theory establishes canonical lifts on the ordinary locus.
present_status: As of November 2026: The intrinsic interpretation is settled; explicit universal formulas require specifying an ordinary locus, coordinate and convergence domain.
attribution: Pierre Deligne / annotating hand not independently identified

statement: The original Ramanujan assertion v5(p(n))≥a,v7(p(n))≥b,v11(p(n))≥c when24n−1 is divisible by5^a7^b11^c is false in the7-part. The corrected7 exponent for b≥1 is floor((b+2)/2); b=0 imposes no7-divisibility. The5- and11-parts retain their stated exponents.
status_on_pages: corrected by himself later: the printed exposition gives the corrected7 exponent after the original conjecture
computation: c63_numerics.py computes p(243),24·243−1=7³·17 and its7-adic valuation2, giving a fully checked counterexample to exponent3. The pentagonal-number recurrence is exact integer arithmetic.
fate: Watson proved the5/7 refinements; Atkin proved the11-power theorem. The copied exposition reports these earlier results; GarvanShomanov2025 supplies checked historical references.
fate_date: Watson1938; Atkin1967; report circulated atBlaricum1966 and printed1968.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established in the corrected form.
attribution: A. O. L. Atkin reporting Ramanujan/Watson

statement: Let j−744=q^−1+Σn≥1 c(n)q^n. The displayed initial coefficients and Lehner divisibility bounds are v2(c(n))≥3a+8 if2^a|n witha≥1; v3≥2b+3 forb≥1; v5≥c+1 forc≥1; v7≥d ford≥1; v11≥e fore≥1. The hypotheses on positive exponents matter; these formulas do not impose all factors on every coefficient.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: Exact q-series from E4³/Δ and integer recurrence are recomputed in c63_numerics.py; finite checked coefficient ranges are recorded and are not proofs of the all-n divisibility theorem.
fate: The exposition attributes these congruences toLehner; Guerzhoy2010 introduction restates the normalized divisibility setting.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established classical congruences; finite numerical checks are labeled as such.
attribution: A. O. L. Atkin reporting Lehner

statement: Modulo13, U13(j−744) is−Δ, so c(13²n)≡8c(13n) and −c(13n)≡τ(n). The Ramanujan τ coefficients satisfy τ(mn)=τ(m)τ(n) for coprime m,n and τ(pn)=τ(p)τ(n)−p11τ(n/p), with the last term0 ifp∤n. These exact Hecke identities explain the congruence recurrence and propagate a vanishing at a prime to multiples coprime to that prime.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: c63_numerics.py recomputes Δ,j and the modulo13 relations on the recorded range; its symbolic Hecke recurrence handles the all-n implication once the modular-form identity is given.
fate: Newman’s congruence is explicitly identified in Guerzhoy2006, corollary1 proof and eq(5). The τ Hecke relations go back toMordell and Hecke.
fate_date: Mordell1917/1919 date in the archival wording retained; exact cited edition must be checked. Newman before1966; Guerzhoy2006.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established. A finite τ table does not prove that τ has no zero.

statement: For j coefficients, the 13-adic recurrence R and normalized Hecke multiplicativity M are asserted for everyα≥1 in the later portion of this exposition. The denominator c(13^α) is a13-adic unit, so tα(n)=c(13^αn)/c(13^α) is well-defined modulo13^α. The paper separately reports finite computations up toα8 and bounds on primes/indices; those are evidence, not the universal theorem.
status_on_pages: stated without proof: proof announced for13; finite experiments described separately
computation: Exact moderate-index congruences and the displayed normalized table are addressed by c63_numerics.py and c63_u13.py. Each output records its modulus and tested index set; the all-α assertion is attributed to the exact later theorem.
fate: Guerzhoy2006 p2 states that the sharp choice M(α)=α is known forj at p13 fromKoike/Katz; this is more precise than the eventual-iteration theorem for all four primes.
fate_date: Atkin–OBrien1967 and Atkin1968; Koike/Katz1970s; explicit later comparison2006.
present_status: As of November 2026: The13 case is established. Do not infer the sharp bound for17,19,23 from the same citation.

statement: A Hecke congruence with a vanishing eigenvalue modulo13^α at a prime propagates zero coefficients along the stated prime divisibility progression, giving a positive-density set of indices. For partitions the half-integral-weight Hecke relation involves p², a Legendre symbol and p^−2,p^−3 factors; it cannot be replaced by the integral-weight j relation. The deleted universal qualifier in the manuscript does not establish the all-α partition conjecture.
status_on_pages: proof sketched for the density implication; the all-α partition assertion remains a conjectural/deleted scope
computation: Propagation is re-derived algebraically from the Hecke recurrence with the coprimality condition. The13-adic partition formula is numerically tested in c63_numerics.py in explicit finite ranges.
fate: GarvanShomanov2025 proves the exact Atkin–OBrien partition Hecke conjecture for everyα≥1 and every auxiliary primep≥5,p≠13 (Conjecture1.2, proved in§4); publication isAdvances inMath490(2026)110840. Earlier Folsom–Kent–Ono/Boylan–Webb results have deeper-iteration bounds.
present_status: As of November 2026: The exact13-power partition conjecture is settled as ofNovember2026. This does not settle every higher-prime speculation on these pages.

statement: The pages report finite-level analogues for17,19,23 and conjecture uniform normalized Hecke congruences asα grows. At29 the two-dimensional U29 action is represented by [[26,3],[14,21]] in the displayed ordered basis; its eigenvectors requireF29² and the slope equation is μ²−8μ+5=0. At31 two components and at37 three are suggested; the dimension floor(p/12) is a heuristic requiring a precise modular-space definition.
status_on_pages: open on the pages beyond the explicitly tested finite ranges
computation: c63_algebra.py checks the matrix, irreducibility of the slope polynomial, determinant11 and M^840=I over F29. Thus M^841=M, the reported Frobenius-sized recurrence; the period is not being claimed to equal841. It does not prove all higher-power lifting claims.
fate: Guerzhoy2006 Theorem1 gives eventual normalized congruences for 13,17,19,23 under its rationality and pole hypotheses. Guerzhoy2010, remark after Theorem1, gives modulus p^(m−C) specifically for j at these four primes, hence an additive threshold in that specialization. It does not extend that quantitative assertion to every F, and neither reference establishes the sharp C=0 assertion for17,19,23 by this argument. The higher-dimensional p=29,31 discussion is separate.
fate_date: 2006; later generalp-adic theory is earlier inSerrePadic1973/Katz1973/Hida.
present_status: As of November 2026: The eventual statement is proved; the exact sharp thresholds and higher-prime formulation must remain separate records.

statement: The weight24 cusp space has dimension2 and its normalized Hecke eigenforms have coefficient fieldQ(√144169). The discussion uses this as an analogy for congruence eigencomponents. Forp5 the stated normalized multiplicativity is modulo5^(3α), a sharper slope-dependent modulus than simply5^α. The p2,3,7 cases andp11 reservations are individually stated, not a theorem for every prime.
status_on_pages: stated without proof; p11 caveat remains
computation: c63_numerics.py builds the weight24 basisΔE4³ andΔ², computesT2, its characteristic polynomial/discriminant and the quadratic coefficient field. The normalized small-prime checks are finite and record denominators before modular inversion.
fate: Guerzhoy2010 proves the small-prime Atkin conjecture with a quantitative congruence modulus; the eigenfield is classical Hecke theory. Its exact slope bounds are kept distinct from the transcription’s initial observations.

statement: For integral weightk in modern notation, Tp acts by a(n)↦a(pn)+p^(k−1)a(n/p), with the standard character factor when present. The manuscript’s dimension−k convention must be converted before using the exponent. A weakly holomorphic modular function with a pole has unbounded pole order under iteratedTp, so its Tp-stable span cannot be finite-dimensional inside a fixed bounded-pole space.

computation: The coefficient action and multiplicativity are checked by formal index manipulation. Pole order grows aspm underTp because the leading pole term cannot cancel against lower-pole summands. This argument does not rule outp-adic limits with varying coefficients.

statement: In Conjecture3 the level prime is q≤23 and the auxiliary Hecke prime p differs from q. For every integer α≥1, the page asks for normalized functions Fα on Γ0(q), holomorphic on the upper half-plane, zero at infinity and with possible poles at0, with integral Fourier coefficients satisfying the stated Hecke congruences modulo q^α and compatibility F_(α+1)≡Fα mod q^α. For each admissible F it asks for a fixed β such that, for every α≥1, Uq^(α+β)F≡k+k_(αβ)Fα mod q^α, with constants k and k_(αβ). The one-dimensional assertion is thus modulo the constants. The next page discusses a distinct larger-prime extension. Literal uniqueness of actual functions Fα is false: at q=13, replacing Fα by Fα+13^αg² with g=(η(13τ)/η(τ))² preserves all residue conditions, normalization and pole restrictions but changes the function.
